No sustained, instrumented response is recorded, and no developmental gain follows any of the four classes. Vigabatrin: 5 children with both endpoints in 4 reports (4 discordant, 1 concordant non-response); these are not independent of the other classes, since three of the five also supply them and all five were on co-therapy. Children with both endpoints, by class, of those exposed: hormonal 3 of 11; ketogenic diet 2 of 12; cannabidiol 1 of 7. Counts only, no percentage (n below 10). A brain-imaging safety signal is recorded beside them in two children (abstract level, a report selected for the finding), so it is not a frequency. No WWOX child is recorded with a developmental gain after a symptomatic improvement. Four children in three reports (two of them in one report) had a partial, transient or clinically-defined improvement with development not progressing; two had neither. That is what the baseline in other genetic and structural early-onset encephalopathies predicts (a responder with poor development is the majority outcome in infantile spasms and near-universal in genetic strata), so it is not by itself a WWOX-specific feature. The comparison holds only as a binary: the baseline uses standardised scores with a cut, every WWOX developmental statement is a clinician narrative, and no WWOX child had a sustained, instrumented response. In two randomised IESS trials (abstract level), arms that raised early spasm cessation by 15 to 19 points showed no demonstrated developmental difference, with about one chance in four of detecting the difference that full mediation would predict. In TSC, two randomised trials of pre-onset prevention changed seizure endpoints without changing development to 36 months; they test prevention before onset, not response after onset. The person-level association (ICISS, abstract level: 15.9 VABS points higher with early cessation) is carried by unknown aetiology and a normal first neurological examination.
